findings.finding: The same ten40-case Joint successes as R1 and native400; three successes recovered relative to R10A, none newly gained over R1.
SA declines against native400 on7 cases versus1 gain, despite11 PC gains versus1 loss. This remains a semantic/physical balance problem.
Internal C is not near-identical across tokens. Lower cosine alone is insufficient evidence of useful physical conditioning.
Inner request binding is selective and preserves differing values, but increases common components. The data do not support calling it fully uniform or a total content collapse.
Request binding has mixed paired impact: versus direct physical read it loses1 SA point and3 PC points across16, but gains2 Joint cases and loses1. It is not established as an overall improvement.
State-value execution has a PC-mean cost but supports two Joint successes; dropping it based only on PC would miss this tradeoff.
Normal C beats the fixed training mean on two Joint cases and one net PC point, with equal mean SA. This supports limited input-specific utility, not comprehensive efficacy.

Visual criteria were corrected against exact prompts: VP027 asks for a smooth round boule, not a mandatory extended kneading sequence; VP034 asks inflation/stretching, not bursting. VP004 lacks clear bending/fracture; VP010 and VP038 have geometric defects.
